item.description:

item.title: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold Ukraine talks after meeting Putin
item.description:
President Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday for diplomatic talks aimed at resuming negotiations between Russia and Ukraine . Why it matters: Kushner and Witkoff traveled to Kyiv right after talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow. This is Witkoff and Kushner's first trip to Ukraine despite months of negotiating with both sides and multiple trips to Russia. Sunday also marked the highest-level visit by a U.S. official to Ukraine since Trump started his second term. Driving the news: U.S. and Russian officials offered positive assessments of Kushner and Witkoff's three-hour meeting with Putin on Saturday. "Kushner and Witkoff are making an effort, and we are making progress," a Russian official said. A White House official said Witkoff, Kushner and Putin discussed "plans for next steps, which will be announced in the coming weeks."…

item.title: French police hunt Renoir thieves after lightning museum heist
item.description:
The Renoir Museum’s alarms went off at 5:48 a.m., but by the time police arrived 5 minutes later, it was already too late — two paintings had been stolen. The thieves broke into the museum on Tuesday, located in the French city of Cagnes-sur-Mer, by cutting through a fence and entering through the main floor, according to the Associated Press . The thieves then cut the bolts holding the four paintings in place and managed to get away with two of the four paintings. Two paintings were left behind in the garden during their escape. Mayor Bryan Masson later revealed that the two stolen artworks are “Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano” and “Young Woman at the Well.” The two abandoned paintings — “Coco Lisant” and “Portrait of Madame Pichon”— were recovered. item.title: Democrats need to win. Here’s the message our research says works
item.description:
Guest Commentary written by Dave Vorland Dave Vorland leads the Blue Horizon Project at Chamber of Progress. He has served in the Obama and Biden administrations and worked in space and missile defense policy. Democrats have long been the party of innovation. John F. Kennedy promised the moon. Bill Clinton and Al Gore embraced the internet revolution. Barack Obama saw technology as a force that could improve lives and modernize government. When HealthCare.gov failed, Obama didn’t declare war on technologists. He brought them in to fix it. That relationship between Democrats and Silicon Valley reflected a shared worldview: optimism about the future, belief in progress and confidence that innovation could expand prosperity and solve problems. After the 2016 presidential election, much of the Democratic Party establishment stopped seeing the tech sector as a strategic American advantage…
